description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2022: Comparative Study of Surrogate Model Methods for Predicting Seismic Structural Response is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Sanjay Govindjee, University of California Berkeley (berkeley.edu). This project is about comparing the accuracy and efficiency of two surrogate modeling methods (Gaussian Process Regression and Probabilistic Learning on Manifolds) for predicting seismic structural responses. The data of this project can be used to further improve the performance of the two surrogate modeling methods at predicting structural responses. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-b6sk-3g29. Keywords: NHERI SimCenter; surrogate modeling; Gaussian Process Regression; Probabilistic Learning on Manifolds; Seismic structural response. Published 2022-08-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
